thread:
maya: getting a 403 after Google OAuth redirect — app returns "invalid_state". User hit this from behind a Cloudflare worker proxy. Works for some users, others fail. Anyone seen state PKCE/session mismatch tied to proxies?

jordan: can you paste the exact callback URL you received and the server log around the time?

maya: here is the redirected URL we got back from Google (redacted):
```
https://app.redwood.ai/auth/callback?code=4/0AbCdEfGhIjKlMn&state=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0...Truncat
```
The state param is clearly truncated (differs from what we stored in the session cookie). Server logs: `auth: oauth callback received, state param len=128, session.state missing or len=0 -> invalid_state`

sre-rotations: that smells like cookie truncation/chunking or a proxy stripping query params. Browser limits cookie size (per-domain ~4096 bytes) and some CF workers or custom middleware will break long cookies into multiple Set-Cookie headers — if our session lookup expects a single cookie value it fails. Do we store full state in cookie?

maya: yes — we store the full PKCE+state blob in an encrypted session cookie (approx 6k when user has lots of flags). Works without the worker. User's CF worker injects some custom Set-Cookie modifications.

ben: quick checklist:
- confirm the session cookie value present on the request to /auth/callback (inspect `Cookie:` header).
- check for multiple `Set-Cookie` headers or `cookie:` truncation in reverse proxy logs.
- validate UA and any header rewriting (X-Forwarded-Proto/Host) — callbacks are sensitive to exact redirect_url.

maya: we captured request headers from the failed run: `Cookie: session=eyJhbGciOiJI...Trunc` (no second chunk). UA: Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh) CF-Worker/1.0.

jordan: repro steps to narrow: 1) enable CF worker in dev, 2) reproduce OAuth flow with increased session payload (add dummy flags until cookie >4k), 3) observe callback `Cookie:` header and querystring `state`. If cookie got truncated, server won't find session.state and returns invalid_state. Can you try with session backed by DB to confirm?

maya: confirmed: switching to server-side session (DB key) fixes the flow. With DB-backed session the state is found and login completes. That strongly indicates cookie truncation.

sre-rotations: recommended fixes:
- short-term: fall back to server-side sessions for customers behind proxies or set cookie size minimization (store only session id + store payload server-side).
- mid-term: change state storage to store SHA256(state) in cookie + full state server-side keyed by short id — prevents storing full blob in user cookie.
- also add instrumentation: log `sha256(session.state)` and `sha256(query.state)` (not the raw state) so we can detect mismatches without leaking secrets.

ben: another mitigation: ensure proxy does not compress/strip Set-Cookie headers or combine multiple cookies incorrectly. For CF worker scripts, watch out for `fetch()` and manual header manipulation — common bug is using `response.headers.set('set-cookie', ...)` which overwrites instead of appending.

maya: patched staging to use DB-backed sessions and added logging of the two SHA256 hashes. Reproduced the original failure on staging with the worker; after patch flow completes. Rolling to prod canary now.

support-bot: escalated to #eng-security for audit and to #eng-platform for follow-up. Reaction :eyes:.

jordan: thanks — can you add minimal repro steps + CF worker snippet that causes the overwrite to the ticket? Put the `fetch()` snippet and the header bug so SRE can triage.

maya: will add to the incident ticket: steps, sample CF worker code (shows `response.headers.set('set-cookie', ...)` mistake), and logs (sha256s).

sre-rotations: after prod canary stabilizes, we'll add a short-runbook for support: indicators (invalid_state + truncated cookie seen in logs), quick mitigation (switch to server DB sessions or short-circuit cookie payload), and long-term engineering task.

ben: follow-up note — also test GitHub OAuth in the same flow; different providers can produce larger states when apps request many scopes. Good catch.

maya: thanks all, deploying canary now, will report back in ~30m with outcome.
